tagline: Empowering businesses with comprehensive HR solutions and services
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the primary operational performance indicator in NSP's business model, as it directly reflects the unit profitability of each managed employee (WSEE), which is at the core of its PEO offering. Pressure on this ratio immediately impacts gross margin and overall profitability.

kpis.name: Gross profit per managed employee
kpis.explanation: Amount of gross profit generated per managed employee each month.
kpis.description: Gross profit per WSEE declined 15% in 2025, primarily due to a 9% increase in benefits costs per participant, despite a 3% price increase.
kpis.signal: Sharp 15% decline year-over-year: pressure on direct costs, especially benefits.

kpis.name: Revenue per managed employee
kpis.explanation: Average revenue generated per managed employee each month.
kpis.description: Revenue per WSEE increased 3% in 2025, thanks to price increases, but insufficient to offset the rise in direct costs.
kpis.signal: Moderate growth in unit revenues despite a tight market.

kpis.name: Managed employees (WSEE)
kpis.explanation: Average number of managed employees each month.
kpis.description: Average WSEEs increased 1% in 2025, reaching 310,089 per month, with middle market segment stable at 26%.
kpis.signal: Very modest volume growth, sign of slowing market penetration.

kpis.name: Gross profit
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenues and direct costs related to PEO services.
kpis.description: Gross profit declined 14% to $900 million in 2025, due to direct cost increases exceeding price increases.
kpis.signal: Marked decline in gross profit in 2025.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Operating income adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA fell 51% to $131 million in 2025, linked to gross margin contraction.
kpis.signal: Severe EBITDA decline, reflecting widespread margin pressure.

kpis.name: Operating expenses
kpis.explanation: Administrative and commercial expenses of the company.
kpis.description: Operating expenses declined 3% to $910 million, notably through savings on professional services and travel.
kpis.signal: Reduction in operating expenses, but insufficient to offset gross profit decline.

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of $6.812 billion in most recent fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of -$0.007 billion in most recent fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA per managed employee
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA divided by the number of managed employees.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA per WSEE fell 52%, declining from $73 to $35 per month between 2024 and 2025.
kpis.signal: More than half decline in unit profitability.

kpis.name: Net income per managed employee
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the number of managed employees.
kpis.description: Net income per WSEE fell 108%, declining from $25 to -$2 per month, sign of strong pressure on profitability.
kpis.signal: Moved into negative territory: unit loss in 2025.

risks.title: Profitability pressure linked to benefits costs
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, with a 9% increase in costs per participant and a $18M deficit in 2025. The language emphasizes direct impact on profitability. The Capital category is heavily weighted here.

risks.title: Dependency on key technology partner (Workday)
risks.score_rationale: Development of HR Scale, the strategic solution, is entirely dependent on Workday. Any delay or issue with Workday is explicitly mentioned as a major operational risk.

risks.title: Sensitivity to wage and labor cost fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: Revenues are linked to payroll costs of WSEEs. The document emphasizes that inflation and workforce composition directly influence both revenues and costs. Significant position in financial analysis.

risks.title: High health insurance claims risk
risks.score_rationale: The document details a partially self-funded model with liability up to $1M per covered employee ($500k in 2026). A major claim could strongly impact liquidity. Technical and precise language indicates an existential risk.

risks.title: Dependency on single health insurance provider
risks.score_rationale: United provides the majority of health coverage. The text explicitly mentions this dependency risk, with implications for rate negotiation and service continuity.

risks.title: Sensitive accounting estimates on future costs
risks.score_rationale: Incurred but not reported (IBNR) estimates are critical and based on subjective judgments. An estimation error would directly impact results, as shown by $11M adjustments in 2025.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence was found in the report.
